comparison: Perfect claim overlap (C38, C39, C42) regarding ATP concentrations and phosphorylation speculation. OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN acknowledging lack of experimental validation. Peer reviewers rate as UNSUPPORTED, directly challenging the relevance given that cellular ATP is millimolar, not micromolar as used in experiments.

Perfect claim overlap (C5, C49, C50, C51) regarding biological relevance and generalizability. OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, acknowledging speculation lacks cellular validation. Peer reviewers rate as UNSUPPORTED, fundamentally questioning physiological relevance and requesting experiments with non-muscle myosin II at physiological ATP concentrations.

High overlap on experimental system design claims (C7-C9, C77-C79). OpenEval finds the MAC system well-characterized and SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers express UNCERTAINTY, questioning whether myosin-II should be tethered independently and whether actin/myosin concentrations reflect in vivo cortex density.

High overlap on model parameters (C60-C71). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED, finding parameters well-established from literature. Peer reviewers also rate as SUPPORTED for the parameters themselves, though they question how these are applied in non-physiological experimental conditions.

Overlap on ATP concentration dependence claims (C10-C12, C75). OpenEval finds these SUPPORTED with systematic observations and adequate sample size. Peer reviewers rate as UNSUPPORTED, strongly criticizing low ATP concentrations as non-physiological compared to millimolar cellular levels.

Overlap on processivity and low ATP claims (C40, C41, C55, C59). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED based on established literature and experimental observations. Peer reviewers rate as UNSUPPORTED, criticizing the approach as creating 'near rigor conditions' that don't reflect physiological behavior.

Overlap on mechanistic model claims (C22-C30). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED, finding the model internally consistent though some aspects inferential. Peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN, questioning whether simulations help the paper and noting that force estimates reflect only 5-6 active heads with >80% in rigor.

Overlap on fragment compaction and foci formation (C14-C16). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED with direct experimental observations across n=21 experiments. Peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN, expressing major concern about lack of quantification despite acknowledging the interesting mechanism.

Overlap on computational simulation claims (C34-C36, C72). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED, finding simulations use well-established parameters and systematically explore parameter space. Peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN, questioning whether simulations lead to testable hypotheses that strengthen the model.

Overlap on single-molecule tracking and processivity (C17-C21). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED with strong quantitative evidence. Peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN, concerned about lack of quantification despite n=21 experiments being reported.

Overlap on background claims about actin cortex (C1, C6). Both OpenEval and peer reviewers rate as SUPPORTED, recognizing these as established background knowledge from literature that appropriately contextualizes the study.

Overlap on simulation velocity results (C73, C74). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED, finding linear velocity-ATP relationship consistent with standard myosin kinetics. Peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN, questioning the simulations' overall contribution to the paper.

Overlap on main findings and mechanism (C3, C4). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED, viewing these as core contributions backed by experiments and modeling. Peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN, questioning simulation utility and noting force estimates reflect only a small fraction of active heads.

Overlap on established myosin properties (C52, C53). Both OpenEval and peer reviewers rate as SUPPORTED, recognizing these as well-established knowledge from prior work that appropriately positions the current study.

Overlap on modeling conclusions (C43-C46). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED, finding simulations successfully demonstrate force generation. Peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN, questioning whether simulations lead to testable hypotheses and noting concerns about the small number of active heads.
Overlap on actin physical properties (C70, C71). Both OpenEval and peer reviewers rate as SUPPORTED, accepting these as well-established literature values appropriately used as model parameters.

Minimal overlap on main finding C2 (ATP-dependent fragmentation). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED as core contribution. Peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN due to lack of quantification, though they acknowledge the mechanism is interesting.

Overlap on trajectory and dwell time claims (C56-C58). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED with strong single-molecule tracking data. Peer reviewers rate as UNSUPPORTED, criticizing the use of free myosin-II in solution forcing rigor conditions.

Minimal overlap on claim C10 (experimental design). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED with systematic observations. Peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN, questioning whether the system reflects in vivo actomyosin density at cell cortex.

Minimal overlap on claim C31 (simulation parameters). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED using well-established physical parameters. Peer reviewers rate as SUPPORTED for the parameters themselves, though context of concerns about non-physiological conditions remains.
